jobs.title: My brother is being held for ransom
jobs.body: Bandits holed up in the old twin towers on the road south, a day out from Baldur’s Gate, have taken my brother Adon and want coin for him. I’d sooner pay honest folk. Fifty gold apiece to bring him home safe, and to teach those thieves some manners. Ask for Rolf at the Flickering Candle.

dm.loot: Roughly 500 gp in coins and gems in the hideout, plus a Potion of Climbing and a Spell Scroll of See Invisibility.
dm.twists: The leader, Mardon Rueh, may offer to hire the party against the Eomane family, which leads to “Blood Night” (chapter 6).

beats.title: Off the Gull's Promise
notes: Two or three minutes. Everyone arrives together on the Gull's Promise: strangers who noticed each other on the crossing but haven't really talked.
They step off the ship onto the cold docks. A quick word with the ship's captain. Throwaway, but the same captain returns later.
Optional line from the captain: "Last time we carried a peddler, she paid in coin I'd never seen before."
Ask each player one question: "Why did you get on that boat?" One answer each, then move on.

beats.title: At the Flickering Candle
notes: They head up to the Flickering Candle. It's empty except for Mags. Each sits at their own table and orders drinks they can't pay for.
Mags drops by each table with one question: "What would you do with a fortune, pet?" One answer each, then move on.
Mags has poured them all drinks. None of them can pay; she's quietly running a tab.
If anyone looks at the notice board, let them read it on the TV.

beats.title: Artum bursts in
notes: The party are the only patrons. Mags shrugs.
Why it's empty: his hired helpers quit this morning after someone fell off a ladder.
Artum, to the party: "You. All of you. You're coming with me."
The offer: 25 gp each for a day's work, plus a seat at the banquet for a job well done.
Mags sells it: "Twenty-five gold? Duck, that's three months of tips."
Artum slaps coins on the bar: "Their tab's paid. Now you owe me."

branches.then: "Fine. Then at least come to the feast as guests. Free food." Either way they're in the banquet hall when the trouble starts.

beats.title: Hang the fir garlands
notes: The ceilings are high and the ladders are rickety. Start the breakage tally now: every failed check that breaks something costs a gold or two off their pay.
Holding the ladder for someone needs no roll and gives the climber advantage.

checks.fail: fall (1d6 bludgeoning) or drop the garland on something breakable

checks.what: hang it so it looks good

beats.title: The scullery china
notes: The scullery is a mess; matching sets are hard to find. Wheeling the crockery back takes strength and care.

checks.fail: mismatched plates, takes twice as long
a stack of plates hits the floor

beats.title: The horses
notes: Several problems at once so players split up. Ask "what do you do?" and pick the roll that fits; a clever idea gets advantage or just works.
Failures make it worse: the runaway horse heads for the hall doors; the carriage tips; the dog steals a ham.
Cut between players at the exciting moment instead of finishing one player at a time.
Ends after 3 successes total (calm) or 3 failures (a guest gets splashed and storms in furious). About 10 minutes.
Bolla shouts tips: "He likes his left ear scratched!"
The first six guests arrive and enter the banquet.

checks.fail: knocked prone in the snow, not hurt

checks.success: automatic if someone offers it food

readAloud: Outside, it's carnage. One draft horse is dragging an entire fir garland down the street like a kite tail. The other has backed a fancy carriage into the fountain, and the carriage is tipping, with a very rich, very loud woman still inside. A mastiff is barking at both of them, delighted. And Bolla is in the middle of it, arms wide, yelling "EASY, EASY!" at no one in particular.

beats.title: Seats or serving duty
notes: Great prep: a seat at the table. Okay: a seat, minus breakage. Bad: serving duty ("You're not sitting. You're carrying.").
Either way, they're in the hall when the pudding attacks.

beats.title: Meet the guests
notes: About 3 minutes. Seat each player next to a named guest, especially the wealthy ones: a pompous merchant, a nervous young noble, a grandmother who won't stop talking. One quick exchange each.
If there's a bard, Artum asks them to play during dinner. The attack can interrupt the song.

beats.title: Artum's toast and dessert
notes: Artum's toast, with a backhanded thanks to the "volunteers" depending on how prep went.
The chef presents dessert proudly. Let it land.

beats.title: The pudding fight
notes: Pudding Gremlin: AC 11, HP 21, Claw +5 (1d4+3). Fire Breath (Recharge 6): 15 ft cone, Dex save DC 11, 2d6 fire, half on success; ready at the start, then roll a d6 at the start of each of its turns, 6 = ready. Death Burst: 5 ft around it, Dex save DC 11, 2d6 fire. Immune to fire. Can sit still and pass as an ordinary pudding.
Create Gremlin (1/day): within 10 ft of an ordinary pudding, turns it into a new gremlin. Put ordinary puddings on the tables; that's the second wave.
Wave 1: two gremlins. Wave 2: start of round 3 or when wave 1 drops, whichever comes first.
Warn a round early: "On the next table, a trifle starts to tremble." Warn before Fire Breath: "Its custard starts bubbling and glowing orange."
Give every round a stake: a pudding lunges at a guest, someone gets cornered.
Scale: struggling party, wave 2 is one pudding; crushing it, add a third. Rough guide: start with two, let only one create a third.
Improvised weapons everywhere (rolling pins, ladles, candelabras): 1d4.

beats.title: Celebration and payday
notes: Narrate the room for 30 seconds, then one quick question per player ("What's the first thing your character eats?").

Pay: great 25 gp each and a seat; okay 20–25 gp minus breakage; bad 15–20 gp after deductions and serving duty. Artum docks it out loud, item by item: "minus three for the plates, two for the garland, and one for my dignity."
Tips from wealthy guests they protected: great 5 gp each, okay 2–3 gp, bad 1 gp.
Everyone gets a tin of Elias's spiced biscuits, no matter what.

beats.title: The chef's confession
notes: Mortified, he explains he bought the recipes from a traveling merchant, and shows the pages: the same symbol on every one.
Answer questions as him; don't push.

beats.title: The recipes won't burn
notes: The chef pushes a page into the party's hands: "I don't want it in my kitchen."
Make sure the party leaves with at least one page.
readAloud: Artum: "Throw the cursed things in the fire!" The chef tosses them in the hearth. The flames curl around the pages and won't take them. They come out cold. Not even singed.

beats.title: Level up
notes: "You're level 2."

beats.title: The stinger
notes: Tell them first: "This is for you, not your characters."
Cut all sound before you start. Read slowly, pause on each "…", drop your voice on the last lantern line. About 45–60 seconds.
readAloud: You're at the Flickering Candle. Warm. Full. Laughing with your new friends about the night you fought off a pudding.
Now… let the view drift. Up, and away from your table. You see yourselves from above. Then the whole tavern: the fire, the music, the happy crowd.
The view drifts toward the door… through it… and everything goes dark.
Slowly, the dark gives way to moonlight. The edge of town, somewhere you don't know. A small cart, hung with tiny lanterns. An old woman beside it. And a child.
The woman hands the child something small. You can't see what. The child jumps with joy.
The woman smiles, waves, and walks her cart toward the Trollbark, into the dark.
And as she goes… one more tiny lantern on her cart flickers to life.
Open your eyes. End of episode one.

beats.title: Roll the stinger
notes: Press Next once they've opened their eyes: the TV plays the stinger (about 25 seconds, no sound) and holds on "End of episode one".
